lead.t: Cystic lesions of the kidneys, pancreas, liver, and epididymis, as well as pheochromocytoma, are frequently associated with von Hippel–Lindau disease.

snip.t: Cystic lesions of the kidneys, pancreas, liver, and epididymis, as well as pheochromocytoma, are frequently associated with von Hippel–Lindau disease.
von Hippel–Lindau disease affects many organs, including the cerebellum, spinal cord, retina, kidney, pancreas, and epididymis.
Association: Von Hippel-Lindau disease — cerebellar, brain stem, retinal, pancreatic, and hepatic cavernous hemangiomas

snip.t: Component of von Hippel-Lindau disease — vascular lesions in cerebellum, brain stem, retina, pancreas, liver

qs.q: A pathologist examines a lesion from a patient with von Hippel-Lindau disease. Which of the following is a characteristic vascular lesion associated with this syndrome?
o: Cavernous hemangioma of the cerebellum or retina
Glomus tumour of the distal digit
qs.e: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is associated with vascular lesions (hemangioblastomas/hemangiomas) in the cerebellum, brain stem, retina, pancreas, and liver. The other options are not specific to VHL.
